label: DomainSpec Formalization Bridge

adopted_contract_fields: node identity, label, concept role, concrete source paths, owner route, candidate status, confidence, challenge contract, residue, and forbidden collapse
relation identity, typed endpoints, direction, owner route, concrete evidence paths, authority effect, value effect, cycle policy, and forbidden collapse
package identity, explicit content boundary, source bindings, human index, schemas, deterministic validator, and append-only receipts
branch as a view rather than an alternative truth source
domain_extensions: project-local formalization-bridge alias mapped to the reusable business-system-bridge ontology type
branch_affinity and explicit business, system, and bridge views
three colocated definition voices: formal, plain-language, and DomainSpec context
semantic_components for the minimum meaning-bearing parts of each concept
separate BusinessMeaning, InterpretationModel, CanonicalProposition, and FormalClaim concepts
typed ownership boundary across domain projects, Define, the formalization package, TDE, providers, and EVF
deferred_items: Define wizard CLI and chat runtime
projection adapter implementation and preservation evidence
FormalClaimSource/v3 adoption or exact v2 projection adapter
forbidden_inferences: CyberAlchemy-v2 provenance is not DomainSpec package authority
ontology creation is not adoption or FormalClaim acceptance
a provider projection is not a new FormalClaim unless meaning, interpretation, proposition, assumptions, or ceiling changes
provider evidence is not business authority or whole-system proof
generated native source is not the canonical JSON source
the legacy Lean snapshot is not current relationship authority

out_of_scope: specific Auth business meaning or FormalClaim

nodes.label: Definition Authority

definition.formal: DefinitionAuthority is the one exact artifact and scope permitted to supply normative definition bodies for a declared claim or package.
definition.plain_language: The exact place allowed to say what the terms mean.
definition.domain_context: For the Auth L0 claim, the accepted definitions-bearing BusinessMeaning is DefinitionAuthority; the graph and envelope are not.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that a purported definition body comes from an artifact outside the declared authority scope.
blocking_questions: Which exact artifact may define this term?

nodes.forbidden_collapse: DefinitionAuthority is not an ontology label, copied envelope, glossary, name match, InterpretationModel, or generated index.

nodes.label: Exact Reference

definition.formal: ExactReference is a tuple of repository path, SHA-256 digest, byte size, and currentness whose fields jointly identify one artifact byte sequence for a declared use.
definition.plain_language: A link that identifies the exact bytes, not just a filename.
definition.domain_context: All current FormalClaim v4 identity, definition, profile, decision, and envelope bindings use this shape.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Recompute the bytes, size, or digest and show that the reference does not identify its declared target.
blocking_questions: Do path, digest, size, and currentness identify the same bytes?

nodes.forbidden_collapse: An ExactReference proves identity and availability only; it does not prove meaning, acceptance, authority, execution, or truth.

nodes.label: Formal Signature

definition.formal: FormalSignature is the explicit finite declaration of the sorts, functions, predicates, constants, arities, parameter sorts, and result sorts used by one CanonicalProposition.
definition.plain_language: The proposition's vocabulary and type sheet.
definition.domain_context: The Auth claim declares AuthorizationRequest, Session, Role, Permission, decision functions, four predicates, and ALLOW and DENY without consulting an InterpretationModel.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show an undeclared symbol, inconsistent arity, or missing sort used by the canonical proposition.
blocking_questions: Is every proposition symbol declared exactly once?

nodes.forbidden_collapse: A FormalSignature declares syntax and types; it does not supply domain definition bodies, provider semantics, or an InterpretationModel.

nodes.label: Evaluation Context

definition.formal: EvaluationContext is a separately identified exact binding that joins one FormalClaim to an optional InterpretationModel, route binding, provider profile, runtime constraints, and a context ceiling for one bounded evaluation.
definition.plain_language: The exact setup used to evaluate a claim this time.
definition.domain_context: The first Auth L0 case has no EvaluationContext yet; one is needed only when a later EVF or provider route evaluates the claim.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a context change that was not given a new context identity or an interpretation incorrectly embedded in FormalClaim identity.
blocking_questions: Which exact claim and optional interpretation does this evaluation use?

residue: No Auth EvaluationContext has been authored because the case remains at L0 claim-draft.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: EvaluationContext is not FormalClaim, business authority, claim admission, provider execution, or evidence.

nodes.label: FormalClaim Envelope

definition.formal: FormalClaimEnvelope is a deterministic non-authoritative consumer view containing one exact FormalClaim reference and the accepted definition bodies selected by its exact definition graph.
definition.plain_language: A convenient definition-complete package for readers and agents.
definition.domain_context: The Auth envelope carries all 20 accepted definition bodies and declares that their interpretation_refs do not become claim dependencies.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a copied definition not selected by the exact graph, a missing selected definition, or an external reference that expands claim meaning.
blocking_questions: Is the envelope definition-complete and non-authoritative?

nodes.forbidden_collapse: The envelope is definition-complete, not globally self-contained; it is not definition authority, FormalClaim identity, InterpretationModel, EvaluationContext, or admission.

nodes.label: Claim Ceiling

definition.formal: ClaimCeiling is the explicit maximum conclusion and authority effect an artifact may assert from its declared inputs and evidence.
definition.plain_language: The strongest thing this artifact is allowed to say.
definition.domain_context: Every FormalClaim, projection, provider result, envelope, and case package states that it proves less than runtime security or production readiness.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show an assertion whose conclusion or authority exceeds the declared inputs and evidence.
blocking_questions: What is the strongest supported conclusion?

nodes.forbidden_collapse: A ClaimCeiling limits assertions; it is not evidence, acceptance, execution authority, or a positive result.

nodes.label: FormalClaim Admission

definition.formal: FormalClaimAdmission is an owner decision over one exact FormalClaim identity that permits only the explicitly named downstream classification, projection, or evaluation boundary.
definition.plain_language: The separate decision that this exact claim may move to the next named step.
definition.domain_context: The Auth v4 claim is a draft and has no FormalClaimAdmission; no v2 projection or obligation may be derived yet.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that a downstream step lacks an exact owner admission for the exact claim or exceeds the named admission boundary.
blocking_questions: Has the owner admitted this exact claim for this exact next boundary?

residue: Auth FormalClaim v4 has no admission.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Admission is not proof, provider selection, execution, publication, deployment, or permission for a successor claim.

nodes.label: Business Meaning

definition.formal: BusinessMeaning = (meaning_id, statement, domain_context, owner, acceptance_ref)
definition.plain_language: The business rule or meaning written in the language used by the domain.
definition.domain_context: A domain project owns this meaning. DomainSpec formalization may reference it but cannot accept or rewrite it by proximity.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that the recorded statement, owner, context, or acceptance binding does not represent the intended domain meaning.
blocking_questions: Who can accept this business meaning?

residue: The candidate BusinessMeaning schema has no domain-owned Auth instance yet.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Business meaning must not be confused with a formal proposition, provider input, test, or provider result.

nodes.label: Interpretation Model

definition.formal: InterpretationModel = (types, predicates, equality, quantifiers, time, currentness, applicability, assumptions, boundaries)
definition.plain_language: The exact explanation of what every important word and condition means before a formal tool sees the rule.
definition.domain_context: It removes ambiguity about equality, time, currentness, scope, assumptions, and the cases the proposition does not cover.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Provide an ambiguous term, missing quantifier, time rule, assumption, boundary, or counterexample that changes the proposition's meaning.
blocking_questions: Are equality, time, currentness, applicability, and assumptions explicit?

residue: The candidate InterpretationModel schema has no accepted Auth instance yet.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: An interpretation model is not merely explanatory prose and is not itself a provider projection.

nodes.label: Canonical Proposition

definition.formal: CanonicalProposition = (representation, representation_digest, semantic_identity, semantic_identity_digest, identity_algorithm)
definition.plain_language: The precise proposition whose meaning must stay stable when different tools receive projections of it.
definition.domain_context: The current FormalClaim v2 input contract already records representation and semantic identity separately.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a semantic change that leaves the recorded proposition identity unchanged, or two equivalent representations that are incorrectly treated as different meanings.
blocking_questions: Which identity algorithm is canonical for the first package profile?

residue: The canonical proposition language remains a profile choice.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: The canonical proposition must not be identified with one provider's generated syntax.

nodes.label: FormalClaim

definition.formal: FormalClaim = (claim_identity, business_binding, definition_binding, formal_signature, canonical_proposition, formal_language_profile, assumptions, claim_ceiling)
definition.plain_language: A versioned formal statement with an explicit vocabulary and exact links to the accepted business definitions it uses.
definition.domain_context: InterpretationModel is not part of the FormalClaim. It may join the claim later through an external evaluation context.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that the claim does not bind exact current business meaning, definition graph, formal signature, proposition, profile, assumptions, and ceiling identities, or that it embeds an InterpretationModel.
blocking_questions: Has every meaning-bearing input been bound by identity and digest?

residue: The v2 and v3 source schemas remain predecessor inputs; the v4 candidate establishes the corrected separation.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A FormalClaim is not an obligation, provider check, test result, proof of implementation, or production guarantee.

nodes.label: FormalClaim Definition Binding

definition.formal: DefinitionBinding(c) = {(c, uses_definition, d) | d is explicitly selected from one exact canonical definition authority}
definition.plain_language: A small graph that lists exactly which accepted definitions a claim uses.
definition.domain_context: The Auth case uses stable definition IDs and JSON pointers from the accepted BusinessMeaning. It never guesses a binding from a symbol name.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a missing, duplicate, stale, inferred, or non-transitively-closed definition edge.
blocking_questions: Does every explicit definition pointer resolve to the accepted authority with the declared digest?

residue: Definition completeness is author-declared and must be independently reviewed; the graph performs no name inference.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: The definition graph is not a copy of definition authority and is not an InterpretationModel.

nodes.label: Formalization Authoring Session

definition.formal: AuthoringSession = (questions, answers, unresolved_questions, draft_output_ref, session_status)
definition.plain_language: The visible CLI or chat conversation used to ask questions and build a draft claim payload.
definition.domain_context: Define may keep questions and answers visible in both CLI and chat. The session helps authors but does not prove or accept the claim.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that the proposed session hides unresolved questions, loses answers, or is treated as accepted meaning or proof.
blocking_questions: Which session states must survive CLI and chat interruption?

residue: The JSON session contract and question flow exist, but the interactive CLI/chat runtime is not implemented.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Wizard state is not canonical business meaning, a FormalClaim acceptance, or formal evidence.

nodes.label: Formal-Language Profile

definition.formal: FormalLanguageProfile = (profile_id, semantics, supported_constructs, unsupported_constructs, projection_rules, provider_bindings)
definition.plain_language: The declared rules for expressing one proposition in a formal language and saying what that language can or cannot preserve.
definition.domain_context: Lean/DTT, TLA/TLC, Alloy, Souffle, SMT, and runtime checks require different profiles; none becomes the owner of business meaning.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Provide a construct, semantic loss, or provider behavior the profile incorrectly marks as supported or meaning-preserving.
blocking_questions: Which proposition language and first provider profile should be created first?

residue: The candidate registry exists, but no profile is admitted for the first Auth case.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A formal-language profile is not a provider result or evidence that a specific projection preserves meaning.

nodes.label: Formalization Projection

definition.formal: Projection(profile, FormalClaim) -> ProviderRepresentation
definition.plain_language: A typed translation of the canonical proposition into the representation expected by one formal provider.
definition.domain_context: Several projections may check one FormalClaim. A projection must state losses and preservation expectations.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Give a source proposition case whose provider representation changes, drops, or invents meaning without an explicit preservation finding.
blocking_questions: What preservation evidence is required for the first projection profile?

residue: Candidate projection and preservation schemas exist, but no route instance or preservation evidence is selected.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A projection is not a new business meaning, an accepted FormalClaim, or provider evidence.

nodes.label: Preservation Binding

definition.formal: PreservationBinding = (claim_digest, profile_digest, projection_digest, preserved_semantics, known_losses, validation_refs)
definition.plain_language: The record of what a projection promises to keep, what it cannot keep, and how that statement was checked.
definition.domain_context: It prevents a provider translation from being treated as equivalent merely because it parses or runs.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Supply a semantic counterexample not covered by preserved semantics, known losses, or the validation references.
blocking_questions: How will semantic equivalence or bounded preservation be tested per profile?

residue: The strength and limits of preservation evidence are profile-specific.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A preservation binding is not universal semantic equivalence or proof of runtime conformance.

nodes.label: Native-Source Bundle

definition.formal: NativeSourceBundle = (profile_ref, media_type, source_text, source_digest, materialization_path)
definition.plain_language: Canonical JSON that carries generated Lean, TLA+, Alloy, Souffle, or other provider source text.
definition.domain_context: Provider-native files may be materialized deterministically from this bundle; the materialized file is generated output.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show nondeterministic materialization, digest mismatch, unsafe path behavior, or a generated file treated as canonical source.
blocking_questions: Which media types and materialization rules belong in the first bundle contract?

residue: The bundle schema exists, but no deterministic materializer or Auth bundle instance exists.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A generated provider file is not the canonical JSON bundle or the proposition owner.

nodes.label: FormalClaim Capability Assessment

definition.formal: CapabilityAssessment = (formal_claim_ref, policy_ref, classification, admitted_route, needs_formal_reasons, currentness, ceiling)
definition.plain_language: A separate policy decision that says which bounded checking route may receive one exact FormalClaim.
definition.domain_context: Validation governance owns the classification. TDE consumes it but does not invent admission or source meaning.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a stale policy or claim binding, a non-total classification, a TDE admission outside executable-bounded, or a provider result placed in the assessment.
blocking_questions: Which exact policy admits the first Auth claim route?

residue: No assessment instance or route admission exists for the Auth case.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A capability assessment is not source meaning, a provider verdict, or proof that an obligation holds.

nodes.label: Neutral Proof Obligation

definition.formal: NeutralObligation = (obligation_id, claim_ref, property, witnesses, counterexamples, vacuity_checks, expected_outcome)
definition.plain_language: A provider-neutral statement of one thing that must be checked for the FormalClaim.
definition.domain_context: TDE derives obligations and cases. The formalization package defines the bridge concept but does not derive them.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that an obligation is provider-specific, is not derivable from the claim, omits negative or vacuity cases, or changes the proposition.
blocking_questions: Which neutral obligation profile will derive the first Auth case?

residue: The candidate neutral-obligation bridge exists, but no TDE implementation or Auth obligation instance uses it.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: An obligation is not the entire FormalClaim, a provider program, or an evidence result.

nodes.label: FormalClaim Lean Binding

definition.formal: FormalClaimLeanBinding = (formal_claim_ref, lean_profile_ref, lean_environment_ref, statement_ref, semantic_digest, preservation_ref)
definition.plain_language: The exact bridge from one FormalClaim proposition to one Lean statement and environment.
definition.domain_context: The theorem route uses this binding instead of converting Lean into an ordinary TDE code renderer.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a statement, profile, environment, or semantic digest that does not match the exact FormalClaim.
blocking_questions: Which exact Lean environment and preservation evidence bind the first theorem route?

residue: No current Auth FormalClaim Lean binding exists.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A Lean statement binding is not a checked theorem, runtime conformance, or release evidence.

nodes.label: EVF Evaluation Request

definition.formal: EvaluationRequest = (claim_ref, route_binding_ref, provider_profile_ref, runtime_ref, policy_ref, request_state, ceiling)
definition.plain_language: The exact bounded question EVF sends to one selected provider.
definition.domain_context: EVF owns actual provider selection and evidence routing after classification and routing candidates exist.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show ambiguous provider selection, stale request inputs, ambient discovery, missing execution policy, or a request that claims an evaluation result.
blocking_questions: Which provider and runtime does EVF select for the first admitted route?

residue: No provider request exists for the Auth experiment.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: An evaluation request is not provider execution, evidence, or an obligation discharge.

nodes.label: Provider Runtime Binding

definition.formal: ProviderRuntimeBinding = (provider, version, digest, input_ref, command, environment, fixtures, limits, outcome_algebra, currentness)
definition.plain_language: The exact tool, command, inputs, environment, fixtures, and limits for one provider run.
definition.domain_context: The provider owns runtime facts. The binding grants no execution or result claim.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show an unpinned provider, ambient command, stale input, unbounded resource, undeclared fixture, or hidden network dependency.
blocking_questions: Which exact runtime is selected for the first provider route?

residue: No runtime binding is selected for the Auth experiment.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A runtime binding is not evidence that the command ran or that the claim holds.

nodes.label: Provider Check

definition.formal: ProviderCheck = (provider_id, route_kind, route_subject_ref, runtime_binding_ref, executable_input_ref, environment_ref, result_domain), where route_subject_ref is exactly one neutral obligation or EVF theorem request
definition.plain_language: One bounded execution for either a TDE-derived obligation or an EVF theorem request, using one exact runtime binding.
definition.domain_context: Lean theorem checks and ordinary execution checks are alternative routes. Each provider checks only the exact route subject and inputs it was given. Unsupported or indeterminate results remain non-pass.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that the provider check lacks exact inputs, environment identity, bounded result semantics, or honest unsupported and indeterminate outcomes.
blocking_questions: Which provider and bounded property are selected for the first vertical?

residue: No provider is selected or executed by this ontology slice.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: A provider check is not business acceptance, a whole FormalClaim proof, or production validation.

nodes.label: Provider Evidence

definition.formal: ProviderEvidence = (check_ref, route_kind, runtime_binding_ref, input_digests, environment_digest, output_digest, status, diagnostics)
definition.plain_language: The exact result and diagnostics produced by one bounded provider check.
definition.domain_context: Execution and theorem evidence bind their exact provider runtime directly. Evidence can support an EVF join only when runtime, inputs, environment, result semantics, and currentness are exact.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Demonstrate missing, stale, ambiguous, unsupported, indeterminate, or non-reproducible evidence inputs or results.
blocking_questions: Which result statuses can EVF consume as bounded pass evidence?

residue: Provider evidence schemas remain provider-owned.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: Provider evidence is not the proposition, business meaning, or proof of unobserved runtime behavior.

nodes.label: EVF Evidence Join

definition.formal: EvidenceJoin = (route_kind, claim_ref, route_subject_ref, route_evidence_refs, runtime_binding_ref, exact_bindings, currentness, status), where the route subject is an obligation for execution evidence or an EVF theorem request for theorem evidence
definition.plain_language: The EVF record that connects exact current evidence back to the exact claim and to either its execution obligation or theorem request.
definition.domain_context: Execution and theorem joins are explicit alternatives. EVF owns this join and must not convert missing, stale, unsupported, indeterminate, or failed evidence into PASS.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show a stale or mismatched claim, route subject, runtime, projection or theorem binding, provider input, environment, or result that the join accepts as current PASS evidence.
blocking_questions: What exact identities must the first evidence join bind?

residue: The route-specific EVF join schema exists, but no executable join implementation or Auth evidence instance uses it.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: An EVF evidence join is not business acceptance, provider semantics, whole-system proof, or production readiness.

nodes.label: Legacy Provider Snapshot

definition.formal: LegacyProviderSnapshot = (source_ref, source_digest, source_system, known_drift, authority_effect=none)
definition.plain_language: An imported formal artifact kept as evidence of an earlier capability and its known limits.
definition.domain_context: DomainSpecEdgeSignature.lean shows a prior Lean checker, but its vocabulary is stale and it is not built or owned as current proof here.

challenge_contract.challenge_response: Show that the snapshot bytes, provenance, drift statement, or authority ceiling are recorded incorrectly.
blocking_questions: Should later generated Lean replace the snapshot or coexist with it as a separate lineage?

residue: A future generation design must decide how to retain this evidence lineage.
nodes.forbidden_collapse: The snapshot must not be treated as current relationship authority, current package implementation, or proof of this ontology.

relations.forbidden_collapse: Capturing an answer does not accept its business meaning.
The interpretation may make meaning precise but may not silently replace the domain statement.
Formalization does not transfer business ownership to the claim or provider.
A definition binding is not an InterpretationModel and contains no canonical definition bodies.
Resolving exact definition addresses does not transfer definition authority to the graph.
The proposition is part of the claim but is not the business binding or claim ceiling.
A profile binding does not mean the provider has run or preserved the proposition.
A new projection does not create a new claim meaning by itself.
Using a profile is not evidence that its provider accepts the projection.
A preservation expectation is not universal equivalence or a provider verdict.
Materialized provider text is generated output, not the canonical proposition.
Classifying a claim does not alter its proposition or establish a provider result.
A projection binding cannot widen the classification, route, domain, or ceiling.
Derivation must not add or weaken proposition meaning.
The Lean binding does not create a second source proposition or a theorem result.
Using a Lean binding does not establish theorem success.
Joining an InterpretationModel for evaluation does not make it part of FormalClaim identity.
Using an EvaluationContext does not change or admit the exact FormalClaim it binds.
A signature declares symbols and types but does not define their business meaning.
A ceiling limits the claim; it is not positive evidence.
The derived envelope is not claim or definition authority.
Admission does not prove, execute, publish, deploy, or admit a successor claim.
Provider selection is not provider execution or a successful result.
A runtime binding does not prove that the provider check ran.
An exact runtime reference does not by itself make evidence current or successful.
Selecting a provider is not a PASS result.
Input availability is not successful provider execution.
Emitted evidence does not automatically become an EVF PASS.
EVF evidence status does not redefine claim meaning.
This execution-route obligation result cannot be generalized beyond its bounded property or substituted for a theorem request.
A theorem-route request result cannot be substituted for an ordinary TDE obligation or runtime conformance.
Joining evidence does not promote provider output into source authority.
An illustrative legacy checker is not a selected current provider binding.

views.purpose: Show the domain-owned meaning that formalization must preserve.
Show profiles, generated provider inputs, checks, evidence, and legacy artifacts without granting them business authority.
Trace business meaning, explicit definition bindings, claim identity, and external evaluation context through capability assessment and provider evidence into the EVF join.

invariants.statement: BusinessMeaning, FormalClaimDefinitionBinding, CanonicalProposition, and InterpretationModel remain distinct. InterpretationModel is not part of FormalClaim.
invariants.formal: FormalClaim(c) implies binds(c, BusinessMeaning) and binds(c, DefinitionBinding) and binds(c, CanonicalProposition) and not contains(c, InterpretationModel).

invariants.statement: A changed business meaning, definition binding, formal signature, assumptions, proposition, or claim ceiling requires a distinct FormalClaim identity; a changed InterpretationModel requires a distinct evaluation context instead.
invariants.formal: ClaimInputs(c1) != ClaimInputs(c2) implies ClaimIdentity(c1) != ClaimIdentity(c2); Interpretation(m1) != Interpretation(m2) implies EvaluationContextIdentity(e1) != EvaluationContextIdentity(e2).

invariants.statement: Adding another provider projection does not create another FormalClaim when meaning-bearing inputs are unchanged.
invariants.formal: MeaningInputs(c1) = MeaningInputs(c2) and only ProviderProjection(c1) != ProviderProjection(c2) implies ClaimIdentity(c1) = ClaimIdentity(c2).

invariants.statement: Every provider projection must have an explicit preservation binding or a typed unsupported result.
invariants.formal: Projection(p) implies exists b: PreservationBinding(b,p) or ProjectionStatus(p)=UNSUPPORTED.

invariants.statement: Unsupported, indeterminate, stale, missing, or failed provider evidence cannot become PASS.
A provider PASS is bounded to its exact claim, obligation, projection, inputs, environment, and result semantics.
invariants.formal: JoinStatus(j)=PASS implies ExactCurrentBindings(j, claim, obligation, projection, inputs, environment, result_semantics).

invariants.statement: The authoring wizard records questions and drafts but does not accept or prove a FormalClaim.
invariants.formal: AuthoringSessionComplete(s) does not imply FormalClaimAccepted(Output(s)) and does not imply FormalClaimProved(Output(s)).

invariants.statement: Canonical JSON native-source bundles remain distinct from generated provider files.
invariants.formal: Materialize(bundle)=file and Digest(file)=bundle.source_digest does not imply file is CanonicalSource.

invariants.statement: Business, system, and bridge views do not create competing truth sources.
invariants.formal: View(v,node) implies projects(v,node) and not owns_authority(v,node).

invariants.statement: The legacy Lean snapshot remains evidence only and cannot establish current package or relationship conformance.
invariants.formal: LegacySnapshotValid does not imply CurrentRelationshipConformant and does not imply FormalizationPackageProved.

invariants.statement: Every FormalClaim definition dependency is an explicit uses_definition edge to an exact canonical definition address; symbol-name inference is forbidden.
invariants.formal: UsesDefinition(c,d) implies ExplicitEdge(c,d) and ExactCurrentAddress(d) and not NameInferred(c,d).

residue.description: Select and review the first canonical proposition profile from the candidate registry for the L0 case.
Implement and test the candidate JSON authoring-session contract in the interactive Define CLI and chat experience.
Instantiate and independently validate the candidate projection and preservation contracts for the first selected provider route.
Implement deterministic materialization and content-digest validation for the candidate native-source bundle contract.
Select a TDE derivation profile and implement the candidate neutral-obligation bridge without changing proposition meaning.
Implement the candidate EVF join and prove its exact-identity, currentness, comparability, and non-pass behavior with fixtures.
Create the first Auth R3 example in Auth Foundation only after the generic ontology and required contracts are reviewed.
Decide whether DS-SFOL has a compatibility role; it is not current semantic authority.

interpretation model is not a canonical proposition
canonical proposition is not provider-native syntax
FormalClaim is not a proof obligation
proof obligation is not a provider check
provider check is not provider evidence
provider evidence is not an EVF PASS
provider PASS is not business acceptance or whole-system proof
wizard completion is not FormalClaim acceptance
generated native source is not canonical JSON source
branch view is not source authority
legacy Lean evidence is not current DomainSpec authority
ontology validation is not formal proof, runtime conformance, security, resilience, release, deployment, or production readiness
